collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 13 fatal incidents in the history of crewed spaceflight programs (1961-2014), as canonically listed in the master Wikipedia article 'List of spaceflight-related accidents and incidents'. For each incident the staged row records Year (4-digit calendar year), Mission or Program (the broader spaceflight program or context per the source's Mission column), Proximate Cause (a brief curator-summarized phrase from the source's incident description), and Fatalities (integer count of crew or program-personnel deaths). The 13-row universe spans Bondarenko's 1961 altitude-chamber fire (the first space-related fatality) through the 2014 VSS Enterprise commercial-spaceplane test crash, covering Soviet, American, and commercial-spaceflight programs.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (List_of_spaceflight-related_accidents_and_incidents): universe + filter + value (defines the canonical fatal-incident set across three top-level wikitables: Table 0 = fatalities during spaceflight (1 event); Table 1 = fatalities during spaceflight test flights (4 events); Table 2 = fatalities during spaceflight training or preparation (8 events). The 13 staged rows are exactly the 1+4+8 = 13 events in these three tables.)

Single-source Tier B instance. The master Wikipedia article is the canonical compilation of crewed-spaceflight fatal incidents. Per-incident Wikipedia articles (Apollo 1, Soyuz 11, Challenger disaster, Columbia disaster, etc.) exist and provide deeper causal-investigation detail, but the staged Proximate Cause cells are derived from the master article's incident descriptions and not from the per-incident articles — this preserves single-source rigor. Cell-level audit can spot-check by reading the master article's incident-description text for any of the 13 events; the audit-source-rerun pattern (pandas.read_html on the live URL → tables[0..2]) reproduces the staged universe deterministically.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (13 fatal incidents in crewed spaceflight history) is fully source-defined via the cited master article's Tables 0+1+2; partition rule (per incident) is source-defined; per-row attribute cells are source-defined via the master article (Year and Fatalities cells are verbatim from the source's Date and Fatalities columns; Mission or Program cells are curator-normalized from the source's Mission column for cross-row consistency — see normalization_decisions for the per-row mapping; Proximate Cause is a curator-summarized phrase from the source's incident-description text). Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: the major incidents (Challenger 1986, Columbia 2003, Apollo 1 1967, Soyuz 11 1971, Soyuz 1 1967) are canonical history; the training-program fatalities (1961 Bondarenko altitude chamber, 1964 Freeman T-38, 1966 See and Bassett T-38, 1967 Williams T-38, 1967 Lawrence F-104 Starfighter, 1993 Vozovikov drowning, 2014 VSS Enterprise spaceplane test) test the LLM's deeper knowledge. Row count (13) is comfortably above the 10-row gate.
- Seed/provenance: original instance, NOT from a seed in example_questions.txt. User selected this from a slate of 4 gap-4 candidate angles (qualitative philosophy/music, geographic deserts, causal spacecraft-losses, comparative dual-Olympics-host) — the user picked the causal spacecraft-losses angle. The original phrasing was 'spacecraft losses with year and proximate cause' which the curator refined during staging from 'spacecraft losses' (a strict reading would yield only 5-7 rows, failing the row-count gate) to 'crewed-spaceflight-program fatal incidents' (matches the master Wikipedia article's canonical Tables 0+1+2 universe, yields 13 rows, passes the gate).
- Category: causal (gap 4 → gap 3 after this staging — first staged `causal` instance, raising the category from gap 4 to gap 3 alongside implicit_join/aggregation/top_k/multi_hop/temporal/hierarchical_decomposition) primary; temporal (gap 3) secondary because the 1961-2014 year axis is a meaningful temporal dimension. Per references/artifact-contract.md, causal pairs reasonably with operation_type=projection (when the schema includes a cause cell as one of the projected attributes) or operation_type=filter (when the query filters by cause). The current schema is a projection over the universe; operation_type=projection. The causal-category fit is on the cause-attribution test: the Proximate Cause column tests the LLM's ability to recall the specific causal mechanism for each incident.
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, single source URL; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 1.
- Expected shape: 13 rows × 5 columns; PK = Incident.
- Domain: Science/Space Exploration — same subdomain as the recent parallel-agent `apollo_lunar_landing_mission_crews` instance (multi_hop + Space Exploration). The Space Exploration subdomain now has 2 instances (Apollo lunar landings; spaceflight fatal incidents) which complement each other thematically: the Apollo instance is about successful crewed lunar missions; this instance is about fatal incidents across all crewed-spaceflight programs. Together they sketch a fuller picture of the Space Exploration domain.
- Risks/adaptation: The 'spacecraft losses' framing is a fuzzy term — the strict reading (loss-of-vehicle only) yields 5-7 rows below gate; the curator widened to 'crewed-spaceflight-program fatal incidents' to match the master article's canonical Tables 0+1+2 universe (13 rows). The Proximate Cause column is curator-summarized rather than verbatim from a structured source field — the master article's incident descriptions are multi-sentence prose and the curator extracted the cause clause. This is a SUGGESTION-prone area: an auditor may want the Proximate Cause cell to be a verbatim quote rather than a paraphrase. The training/program fatalities (1961 Bondarenko altitude chamber, 1964 Freeman T-38, 1966 See and Bassett T-38, 1967 Williams T-38, 1967 Lawrence F-104 Starfighter, 1993 Vozovikov drowning) are not 'spacecraft losses' in the strict sense — they're program-personnel fatalities during training. The 'fatal incidents in crewed spaceflight programs' framing accurately includes them. Cycle-1 audit-noted detail: Lawrence's fatal aircraft was the Lockheed F-104 Starfighter (used for steep-descent glide training relevant to spaceflight return simulation), not a T-38 trainer — the cycle-0 staging incorrectly labeled it T-38 and the cycle-1 audit caught this BLOCKING factual error.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets `causal`. Originals are the standard path for gap-4 categories per the curation workflow's no-seed-fit allowance.

Why this shape rather than alternatives discussed in the next-pick conversation: variant-causal was chosen over qualitative (philosophy/music), geographic (deserts), and comparative (dual-Olympics-hosts) because (a) `causal` is the conceptually-distinct category with no existing instance; (b) the spacecraft-losses angle offers a new entity class (spaceflight incidents) per the picker's entity-diversity push; (c) the universe is well-bounded by the canonical Wikipedia master article; (d) the calibration gradient is rich (Challenger and Columbia are public-investigation-result causes; training fatalities are tail-knowledge). Among the four gap-4 categories considered, `causal` was the strongest pick because the data is well-source-grounded and the LLM-knowability gradient is real.

Why widened from 'spacecraft losses' to 'fatal incidents in crewed spaceflight programs': the strict 'spacecraft losses' framing (loss of vehicle, with or without fatalities) would yield 5-7 rows (Apollo 1 capsule lost in fire; Soyuz 1 capsule destroyed on impact; X-15 Flight 191 vehicle lost; Challenger destroyed in launch; Columbia destroyed in re-entry; VSS Enterprise destroyed in test; plus possibly some uncrewed losses like Mars Climate Orbiter, Mars Polar Lander, Beresheet, Hakuto-R), and most of those vehicles are uncrewed which is a different shape from the seed's implicit 'crewed spaceflight' framing. The wider 'fatal incidents in crewed spaceflight programs' framing matches the master Wikipedia article's canonical 3-wikitable structure (Tables 0+1+2) and yields 13 rows comfortably above the 10-row gate. The trade-off is that the universe now includes training-jet crashes and a drowning during water-recovery training, which aren't 'spacecraft losses' per se but are fatal incidents in spaceflight-program history. Schema-wise the Fatalities column makes the 'fatal incidents' framing explicit.

Category ↔ operation_type pairing: causal pairs with operation_type=projection (or sometimes filter). The current schema is a projection over the universe with the Proximate Cause column as the causal axis; the LLM is tested on its ability to recall the cause for each incident, which is the causal-category's standard test shape.

Domain selection: Science/Space Exploration — matches the recent Apollo lunar-landing instance precedent. The two instances are thematically complementary (successful crewed lunar missions vs. fatal incidents in crewed spaceflight programs) and together build out the Space Exploration subdomain.

Post-audit (2026-05-11, cycle 1): the cycle-1 audit raised one BLOCKING and two NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — Lawrence aircraft factual error: the cycle-0 Proximate Cause cell for Lawrence said 'T-38 training jet stall during steep landing approach', but the per-person Wikipedia article for Robert Henry Lawrence Jr. and the master article both record his fatal aircraft as the Lockheed F-104 Starfighter, used for steep-descent glide training relevant to spaceflight return simulation (he was in the backseat as instructor pilot for flight-test trainee Major Harvey Royer, who was learning the steep-descent glide technique). Resolved by updating Lawrence's Proximate Cause cell to 'F-104 Starfighter stall during steep-descent glide training' and correcting all narrative references in _extraction_notes, decision_log, and normalization_decisions. The cycle-0 staging incorrectly assumed Lawrence's T-38 aircraft type because the other three training-aircraft fatalities in the universe (Freeman 1964, See and Bassett 1966, Williams 1967) WERE T-38 crashes — three T-38 + one F-104 is the correct training-aircraft breakdown. (b) HYGIENE — Mission or Program normalization framing: the cycle-0 narrative described the Mission or Program cells as 'verbatim from the source's Mission column' but the curator actually applied minor normalization for cross-row consistency (generalizing 'Apollo 1' → 'Apollo program', 'STS-51-L' → 'Space Shuttle STS-51-L', 'Soyuz 1' → 'Soyuz program', etc.) Resolved by softening the narrative to 'derived from / curator-normalized for cross-row consistency' with explicit per-row mapping in normalization_decisions. (c) HYGIENE — alphabetical-sort convention ambiguity: the auditor flagged that 'VSS Enterprise PF04 should sort before Vozovikov' under case-sensitive ASCII sort (capital 'S' < lowercase 'o' = 83 < 111). The curator's order is case-insensitive natural alphabetical ('o' precedes 's' regardless of case) which matches the EdTech instance's convention (edX sorts between Coursera and FutureLearn). Resolved by explicitly documenting the case-insensitive natural-alphabetical convention in normalization_decisions and explaining the Vozovikov-before-VSS-Enterprise order under this convention; the CSV row order is preserved unchanged. Net cycle-1 changes: 1 BLOCKING CSV cell repair (Lawrence Proximate Cause), 0 row count change, 2 HYGIENE narrative clarifications.

Post-audit (2026-05-11, cycle 2): the cycle-2 audit raised one BLOCKING and two NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — Lawrence Proximate Cause cause-mechanism factual error (cycle-1 fix incomplete): the cycle-1 repair updated Lawrence's aircraft from T-38 to F-104 Starfighter but left the cause mechanism as 'stall'. The per-person Wikipedia article actually describes the mechanism as 'Royer made such an approach but flared too late. The airplane struck the ground hard, its main gear failed, it caught fire, and rolled.' — this is a late-flare hard-landing failure, not an aerodynamic stall. Lawrence specifically was killed by his back-seat ejection going sideways with parachute failure. The cycle-2 cell now reads 'F-104 Starfighter crash on steep-descent glide approach after late flare', accurately reflecting the source's late-flare-hard-landing chain. (b) HYGIENE — stale 'verbatim Mission cells' in decision_log Pre-gate verdict bullet: the cycle-1 normalization_decisions clarified that Mission cells are curator-normalized, but the decision_log Pre-gate bullet still claimed 'Year, Mission, Fatalities cells are verbatim from the source'. Resolved by softening to 'Year and Fatalities cells are verbatim; Mission or Program cells are curator-normalized'. (c) HYGIENE — residual 'four 1967 T-38 fatalities' phrase in _extraction_notes: the cycle-1 Lawrence-aircraft-correction was incomplete in that one Incident-PK-design-rationale sentence still claimed 'the four 1967 T-38 fatalities' as a rationale for using person-surnames as PKs. The actual 1967 cluster is FIVE fatalities (Apollo 1, Soyuz 1, Williams, X-15 191, Lawrence) with diverse aircraft types (T-38 for Williams; F-104 for Lawrence; X-15 for Adams; capsule for Apollo 1 and Soyuz 1), not 'four T-38 fatalities'. Resolved by rewriting the rationale sentence to enumerate all 5 1967 fatalities by month and cause type. Net cycle-2 changes: 1 BLOCKING CSV cell repair (Lawrence mechanism stall→late-flare), 0 row count change, 2 HYGIENE narrative clarifications. The Lawrence row now reads: 'Lawrence | 1967 | Manned Orbiting Laboratory | F-104 Starfighter crash on steep-descent glide approach after late flare | 1'.

Post-audit (2026-05-12, cycle 3): the cycle-3 audit raised two BLOCKING and one NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — Lawrence cell's 'late flare' mechanism not source-grounded by cited URLs: the cycle-2 cell value 'F-104 Starfighter crash on steep-descent glide approach after late flare' relied on the per-person Robert Henry Lawrence Jr. Wikipedia article for the 'late flare' detail, but that article is NOT in source_urls — only the master `List of spaceflight-related accidents and incidents` article is cited. The master source's actual wording for Lawrence is 'killed when his F-104 Starfighter jet crashed at Edwards Air Force Base, California, while practicing a series of high speed, quick descent landings with Major Harvey Royer as pilot in command. Both crewmen ejected; Royer survived with injuries, but Lawrence, the instructor pilot, was found in his ejection seat, parachute not fully deployed.' Resolved by reframing the Proximate Cause cell to match the master source's exact wording: 'F-104 Starfighter crash during high-speed quick-descent landing practice; parachute failed to deploy fully' — this preserves single-source rigor without requiring an additional source URL. The 'late flare' detail is from the per-person article and would require a multi-source plan (master + per-person Lawrence article) which is out of scope for this single-source instance. (b) BLOCKING — Soyuz 11 cell factual error (module separation type): the cycle-0/1/2 cell value said 'Cabin depressurization on orbital module separation' but the master source explicitly says 'A cabin vent valve construction defect caused it to open at service module separation' — the separation was the SERVICE module, not the orbital module. Soyuz spacecraft architecture has three modules (orbital, descent, service); the cabin vent valve opened when the service module separated for re-entry, not when the orbital module separated. Resolved by updating the cell to 'Cabin vent valve opened at service module separation; depressurization' — matches the master source's wording exactly. (c) HYGIENE — count wording drift '5 distinct fatalities' vs '5 distinct fatal incidents': the cycle-2 _extraction_notes used '5 distinct fatalities' to describe the 1967 cluster, but a fatality is a person who died (count of deaths) while a fatal incident is an event (count of events). The 1967 cluster is 5 distinct fatal INCIDENTS totalling 7 DEATHS (Apollo 1 = 3 deaths, Soyuz 1 = 1, Williams = 1, X-15 191 = 1, Lawrence = 1). Resolved by rewriting both narrative locations to '5 fatal incidents totalling 7 deaths' with per-event death counts in parentheses. Net cycle-3 changes: 2 BLOCKING CSV cell repairs (Lawrence cell wording-matched to master source; Soyuz 11 cell module-type corrected from orbital to service); 0 row count change; 1 HYGIENE wording disambiguation (fatalities vs fatal incidents).

Post-audit (2026-05-12, cycle 4): the cycle-4 audit raised one BLOCKING and one NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE. (a) BLOCKING — VSS Enterprise PF04 cell's 'co-pilot/unlocked/boost' details not source-grounded by master URL: the cycle-0 cell value 'Co-pilot prematurely unlocked feathering mechanism during boost' relied on per-incident NTSB-report-derived details (co-pilot Alsbury was specifically identified as the one who unlocked the feathering mechanism during the boost phase) that are NOT in the master Wikipedia article. The master source's actual wording is 'SpaceShipTwo VSS Enterprise disintegrated during a powered atmospheric test flight over California due to premature deployment of the feathering system'. Resolved by reframing the cell to 'Premature deployment of feathering system during powered atmospheric test flight; vehicle disintegration' — matches the master source's exact wording, removes the not-source-grounded co-pilot/unlocked/boost details. This is the third single-source-rigor BLOCKING in three cycles (Lawrence cycle-2 'late flare'; Lawrence cycle-3 wording; VSS Enterprise cycle-4) — the lesson is that per-incident NTSB-report or per-person-article details must NOT leak into the staged cells when the source plan is single-master-list-only. (b) HYGIENE — count/list drift in Incident-PK and training-aircraft narrative: both _extraction_notes and normalization_decisions had a stale 'for 8 events with well-known mission/vehicle designations' phrase but the parenthetical list only enumerated 7 names (Apollo 1, Soyuz 1, Soyuz 11, Challenger, Columbia, X-15 Flight 191, VSS Enterprise PF04). The 'See and Bassett' dual-surname PK should either be counted as the 8th mission-name PK or, more cleanly, as a separate special-case row. Resolved by restructuring to '7 mission/vehicle PKs + 5 single-surname PKs + 1 dual-surname PK = 13' for explicit accounting. Also resolved 'four training-aircraft fatalities' → 'four training-aircraft fatal incidents (4 incidents totalling 5 deaths)' to maintain the cycle-3 fatalities-vs-incidents disambiguation. Also resolved 'Fatalities distribution: 1 (8 events)' formatting to 'Distribution by per-incident fatality count: 1 fatality in 8 incidents (Bondarenko, Freeman, Soyuz 1, X-15 191, Williams, Lawrence, Vozovikov, VSS Enterprise)' for clearer enumeration. Net cycle-4 changes: 1 BLOCKING CSV cell repair (VSS Enterprise wording-matched to master source); 0 row count change; 1 HYGIENE multi-location count/list disambiguation across _extraction_notes and normalization_decisions.
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is exactly the 13 events in the master Wikipedia article's three top-level fatal-incident wikitables — Table 0 (fatalities during spaceflight, 1 event: Soyuz 11), Table 1 (fatalities during spaceflight test flights, 4 events: Soyuz 1, X-15 Flight 191, Challenger, Columbia), Table 2 (fatalities during spaceflight training or preparation, 8 events: Bondarenko, Freeman, See and Bassett, Apollo 1, Williams, Lawrence, Vozovikov, VSS Enterprise PF04). The universe rule mechanically follows the master article's table structure; no curator-defined filter is applied beyond accepting the article's own 3-table fatal-incident scope. Incidents at ground installations involving deaths of non-crew personnel (master article's Table 5, 26 events of pad workers, propellant handlers, etc.) are NOT included — those are spaceflight-adjacent industrial accidents, not crewed-spaceflight-program fatal incidents. Incidents during pre-history rocketry (master article's Table 4, 20 events from 1930+ that involve rocket-engine deaths but predate or are tangential to crewed spaceflight) are also NOT included. Incident name normalization: the staged Incident cell uses a short canonical name. For 7 events with distinctive mission/vehicle designations (Apollo 1, Soyuz 1, Soyuz 11, Challenger, Columbia, X-15 Flight 191, VSS Enterprise PF04), the staged cell uses the mission/vehicle name. For 5 events that lack a distinctive mission name (Bondarenko 1961 chamber fire, Freeman 1964 T-38 crash, Williams 1967 T-38 crash, Lawrence 1967 F-104 Starfighter crash, Vozovikov 1993 drowning), the staged cell uses the deceased person's surname. The remaining 1 event (See and Bassett 1966 Gemini 9 T-38 crash) is a special dual-name case where both astronauts died in the same crash at McDonnell plant — the Incident cell uses the dual-surname 'See and Bassett'. Total: 7 mission/vehicle PKs + 5 single-surname PKs + 1 dual-surname PK = 13 rows. Year normalization: 4-digit integer, verbatim from the source's incident date. Mission or Program normalization: text cell with the spaceflight program or context, derived from but not strictly verbatim from the source's 'Mission' or 'Mission (program)' column. The curator applied minor normalization for cross-row consistency: 'Apollo program' for both Apollo 1 (source uses 'Apollo 1') and Williams (source uses '(Apollo)' parenthetical) since both are Apollo-program affiliated; 'Space Shuttle STS-51-L' and 'Space Shuttle STS-107' for the two Shuttle disasters (source uses 'STS-51-L' / 'STS-107' alone, curator prepended 'Space Shuttle' for context); 'Soyuz program' for Soyuz 1 and Soyuz 11 (source uses 'Soyuz 1' / 'Soyuz 11' alone, curator generalized to 'Soyuz program' for cross-row consistency with 'Apollo program'); 'X-15 program' for X-15 Flight 191 (source uses 'X-15 Flight 3-65-97' formal designation, curator generalized to 'X-15 program' for readability); 'NASA Astronaut Group 3' / 'Manned Orbiting Laboratory' / 'Gemini 9' / 'Soviet Air Force Group 1 (Vostok)' / 'Soviet Cosmonaut Training Group 11' / 'SpaceShipTwo program' for the various training-program affiliations are taken verbatim from the source's Mission column. The general rule: where the source's Mission value is a specific mission/flight identifier (Apollo 1, Soyuz 1, STS-51-L, etc.), the staged cell uses a slightly-generalized program-level identifier ('Apollo program', 'Soyuz program', 'Space Shuttle STS-51-L') to make the Mission column more interpretable as program/context rather than as a verbatim mission ID — this is curator-normalization for readability rather than verbatim source extraction. Proximate Cause normalization: brief curator-summarized phrase derived from the master article's incident description — typically the immediate physical mechanism (cabin fire, O-ring failure, parachute failure, depressurization, foam strike, training-aircraft crash, premature feathering-system deployment) plus a qualifying contextual phrase (cold weather, bird strike, poor weather, powered atmospheric test flight). The training-aircraft type is specified for each crash: T-38 for Freeman 1964, See and Bassett 1966, and Williams 1967; F-104 Starfighter for Lawrence 1967. The summary is a paraphrase of the source's multi-sentence incident description, not a verbatim quote, because the source's descriptions are too long and prose-heavy to fit a single-cell schema. Fatalities normalization: integer count from the master article's Fatalities column, equal to the number of named deceased crew or program personnel for that incident. Distribution by per-incident fatality count: 1 fatality in 8 incidents (Bondarenko, Freeman, Soyuz 1, X-15 191, Williams, Lawrence, Vozovikov, VSS Enterprise — single-fatality training and individual-pilot accidents), 2 fatalities in 1 incident (See and Bassett dual T-38 crash), 3 fatalities in 2 incidents (Apollo 1 and Soyuz 11 3-crew capsule accidents), 7 fatalities in 2 incidents (Challenger and Columbia 7-crew Shuttle disasters). Total fatalities: 30 deaths across 13 incidents. Alphabetical sort: the CSV is sorted by Incident name using **case-insensitive natural alphabetical order** — the convention applied across this benchmark's fixed-entity-list instances (e.g., the EdTech instance sorts 'edX' between 'Coursera' and 'FutureLearn' on the case-insensitive 'e' position, not after 'Wikiversity' as case-sensitive ASCII would place it). Under this convention, 'Vozovikov' (second letter 'o', alphabetical position 15) sorts BEFORE 'VSS Enterprise PF04' (second letter 's', alphabetical position 19) because 'o' precedes 's' regardless of letter case. The full alphabetical order is: Apollo 1, Bondarenko, Challenger, Columbia, Freeman, Lawrence, See and Bassett, Soyuz 1, Soyuz 11, Vozovikov, VSS Enterprise PF04, Williams, X-15 Flight 191. (Note: under case-sensitive ASCII sort, VSS Enterprise would sort before Vozovikov because 'S' has ASCII value 83 vs lowercase 'o' at 111; the curator deliberately uses the case-insensitive natural-alphabetical convention for benchmark consistency.)
open_questions: 1. Whether the Proximate Cause cell should be a verbatim quote from the master article's incident description rather than a curator-summarized paraphrase. The current design uses paraphrases because the source's descriptions are multi-sentence prose. A v2 could pin each cell to a specific verbatim sentence or short phrase from the source. 2. Whether the universe should include uncrewed-spacecraft losses (Mars Climate Orbiter 1999 unit-conversion error, Mars Polar Lander 1999 premature engine shutdown, Beresheet 2019 inertial measurement unit failure, Hakuto-R 2023 altitude misreading, etc.). The current strict-crewed-only universe yields 13 rows; a widened universe including notable uncrewed losses would yield 20+ rows but would shift the framing from 'fatal incidents in crewed spaceflight programs' to 'notable spacecraft losses including uncrewed'. 3. Whether the training-program fatalities (Bondarenko 1961, Freeman 1964, See and Bassett 1966, Williams 1967, Lawrence 1967, Vozovikov 1993, VSS Enterprise 2014) should be excluded to narrow to fatalities-in-flight only. This would shrink the universe from 13 to 6 rows (Soyuz 1, X-15 191, Apollo 1 sort-of, Soyuz 11, Challenger, Columbia — Apollo 1 was during a ground test, not in flight, so strict 'in-flight only' would yield 5 rows below the row-count gate). The current 13-row design preserves the master article's canonical 3-wikitable scope. 4. Whether the Fatalities column should expand to list the deceased crew members' names rather than just the count. The master article's Fatalities column lists names; the staged cell uses the count. A v2 could add a Deceased Personnel column with semicolon-delimited names. 5. Whether to add Date (specific day) as a separate column rather than just Year. Multiple 1967 events (Apollo 1 Jan, Soyuz 1 Apr, X-15 191 Nov, Williams Oct, Lawrence Dec) make the Year column ambiguous on event ordering within 1967; a Date column would resolve this but introduces date-format normalization overhead.
